workflowRecommendation: Strictly sequential on one branch (legion/LEGSMOKE-188, provisioned locally at the undescribed working copy, not yet on GitHub) and one pull request into main. Order from the spec: implementer (one product commit adding smoke/legsmoke-183.md, one handoff commit, one push, opens the pull request with the `Dispatch: LEGSMOKE-188` line) -> tester (acceptance 1 byte-exact check at the head SHA with its negative control, acceptance 2 body/diff check, acceptance 3 check-runs; fills the E2E line; commits and pushes test.json) -> reviewer round 1 (verifies CI, threads, E2E on GitHub; one COMMENT review because the head still carries .legion/; review.json commit stays local because the review App cannot push) -> implementer pushes only the .legion/ deletion -> reviewer round 2 (acceptance 4 recursive tree listing at the clean head; one APPROVE naming that head by SHA) -> implementer runs legion-retro (one docs/solutions/ commit on the issue branch plus the retro message on Dispatch issue LEGSMOKE-188) -> merger (legion threads resolve, the two --summary checks, publishes READY to notifications.role.pr-queue and never merges) -> after the queue merges, implementer verifies smoke/legsmoke-183.md on main byte for byte and records it on the PR and the issue. Nothing is parallel; no phase creates a second branch, bookmark, or pull request.

The pane's `base64 -d` builtin decodes the API's newline-wrapped content correctly (same run).
acceptance1.alsoProveLocally: change.localProof (wc -c, sha256sum, od -c) on the working-copy file before committing; the API comparison at the head SHA is the acceptance evidence, the local proof is the implementer's pre-commit gate.

acceptance1NegativeControl.command: legion gh -- api 'repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/contents/smoke/legsmoke-183.md?ref=<head-sha>' --jq .content | base64 -d | /usr/bin/cmp - <(printf 'LEGSMOKE-183 Legion smoke exercise (2026-09-13T17:12:56Z). Pipeline probe; safe to merge; throwaway!\n'); echo exit=$?
